event.details: Mudgala says Jambū’s ruler has nine sons Nābhi, Kimpuruṣa, Hari, Ilāvṛta, Hiraṇmaya, Kuru, Ramya, Bhadrāśva, Ketumāla; he gives each an eponymous region. Father is called Jambū ruler here, not named; prior 10.4 identifies him as Āgnīdhra. The SEVEN Priyavrata sons, distinct from these nine grandsons, then enter forest, perform tapas, become Gaṇapatyas/Brahman-knowers and at the end attain Gaṇeśa’s abode without return through yoga-nondifference.

evidence.paraphrase: Priyavrata has10 powerful dharmic sons: Āgnīdhra,Idhmajihva,Yajñabāhu,Vīra,Hiraṇyaretas,Savana,Ghṛtapṛṣṭha,Medhātithi,Vītihotra,Kavi. Kavi/Savana/Vīra do not desire rule; he appoints seven others to Jambū/Plakṣa/Śālmala/Kuśa/Krauñca/Śāka/Puṣkara respectively. He then goes to forest, receives yoga from Nārada, becomes Gaṇapatya and finally Gaṇeśa-formed through yoga; source calls no comparable king past/future. Mother not specified here.
